title: ARIES Recovery
overview:
In this project you will implement the **ARIES** (Algorithms for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics) recovery algorithm — the industry-standard approach to crash recovery in database systems.

The key insight behind ARIES is the **Write-Ahead Log (WAL)** protocol: every change to the database is first recorded in a sequential log file before the change is applied to the actual data pages. On crash, the system can recover to a consistent state by replaying the log.

ARIES recovery has three phases:

1. **Analysis**: Scan the log from the last checkpoint to determine which transactions were active at crash time (Active Transaction Table) and which pages may be dirty (Dirty Page Table).

2. **Redo**: Starting from the earliest dirty page's recLSN, replay all logged changes forward to bring the database to its exact pre-crash state — including uncommitted changes.

3. **Undo**: Roll back all uncommitted transactions by following each transaction's `prev_lsn` chain backward, writing **Compensation Log Records (CLR)** for each undone operation. CLRs ensure that undo is idempotent — if the system crashes during recovery, re-running recovery produces the same result.

You will implement two components: the **LogManager** (WAL writing and reading) and the **RecoveryManager** (the three ARIES phases).

tasks.title: Log Manager
tasks.description:
The `LogManager` writes log records to a WAL file and reads them back for recovery. Each log record is assigned a monotonically increasing **LSN** (Log Sequence Number). Records for the same transaction are linked via `prev_lsn` pointers, forming a chain that the Undo phase follows backward.

**WAL Protocol:** The log for a page must be flushed to disk BEFORE the dirty page is written to disk. COMMIT records are always force-flushed immediately.

**Log file format:** Each record is stored as `[4-byte length][serialized record]`.

functions.name: AppendLog(LogRecord& record) → lsn_t
functions.description: Assign an LSN to the record, link it to the transaction's previous record via `prev_lsn`, serialize it, and append to the in-memory log buffer. For COMMIT and CHECKPOINT records, immediately flush the buffer to disk (force-write).
hints: Assign `record.lsn = next_lsn_++`.
Set `record.prev_lsn = last_lsn_[record.txn_id]`, then update `last_lsn_[txn_id] = record.lsn`.
Serialize with `record.Serialize()` and prepend a 4-byte length.
Append to `log_buffer_`.
If type is COMMIT or CHECKPOINT, call `FlushLog(record.lsn)`.

functions.name: FlushLog(lsn_t up_to_lsn)
functions.description: Write the entire in-memory log buffer to the log file on disk, update `flushed_lsn_`, and clear the buffer.
hints: Seek to end of file with `seekp(0, ios::end)`.
Write `log_buffer_` contents.
Call `flush()` for durability.
Clear `log_buffer_` and set `flushed_lsn_ = up_to_lsn`.

functions.name: ReadAllLogs() → vector<LogRecord>
functions.description: Read the entire log file and deserialize all log records. Used during recovery to reconstruct the full log history.
hints: Seek to end to get file size, then read entire file into a byte buffer.
Loop: read 4-byte length, then deserialize `length` bytes with `LogRecord::Deserialize()`.
Stop when end of buffer is reached.

tasks.title: Recovery Manager — Analysis Phase
tasks.description:
The Analysis phase scans the log from the last checkpoint (or the beginning if no checkpoint exists) to reconstruct two tables:

- **ATT (Active Transaction Table):** `txn_id → lastLSN` for transactions that were running at crash time. Transactions that committed or aborted are removed.

- **DPT (Dirty Page Table):** `page_id → recLSN` where recLSN is the LSN of the first log record that dirtied the page. This tells the Redo phase where to start replaying for each page.

functions.name: Analyze(const vector<LogRecord>& logs)
functions.description:
Scan log records and build the ATT and DPT.

For each record:
- **BEGIN**: add `txn_id` to ATT with `lastLSN = record.lsn`
- **COMMIT / ABORT**: remove `txn_id` from ATT
- **UPDATE / CLR**: add/update `txn_id` in ATT; if `page_id` not in DPT, add it with `recLSN = record.lsn`
- **CHECKPOINT**: initialize ATT and DPT from the checkpoint's stored tables, then continue scanning
hints: Find the last CHECKPOINT by scanning backward.
Initialize ATT/DPT from checkpoint data if found.
Scan forward from checkpoint+1 (or beginning if no checkpoint).
Use `att_[txn_id] = lsn` for ATT updates.
Use `dpt_.find(page_id) == dpt_.end()` to check before adding to DPT.

functions.name: Recover()
functions.description: Run the three ARIES phases in order: `Analyze()`, then `Redo()`, then `Undo()`.
hints: The order is the algorithm; none of the three works out of place.

tasks.title: Recovery Manager — Redo Phase
tasks.description:
The Redo phase replays all changes from the log to bring every page to its exact pre-crash state. It starts from the minimum `recLSN` across all entries in the DPT.

For each UPDATE or CLR record:
1. **Skip** if the page is not in the DPT
2. **Skip** if `record.lsn < DPT[page_id].recLSN`
3. **Skip** if the page's current `pageLSN >= record.lsn` (already applied — this is why pages store pageLSN)
4. Otherwise, **apply the `after_image`** to the page at the specified offset and set `pageLSN = record.lsn`

The pageLSN check (step 3) is what makes redo idempotent — it's safe to redo a record that was already applied.

functions.name: Redo(const vector<LogRecord>& logs)
functions.description: Replay logged changes for dirty pages. Apply `after_image` to each page that needs it.
hints: Compute `min_rec_lsn = min(dpt_[*].recLSN)`.
Skip records with `lsn < min_rec_lsn`.
For each qualifying record: `FetchPage`, check `pageLSN`, apply if needed.
Use `memcpy(page->GetData() + offset, after_image, length)`.
Don't forget to `UnpinPage` with dirty=true after modification.

tasks.title: Recovery Manager — Undo Phase
tasks.description:
The Undo phase rolls back all transactions that were active at crash time (those remaining in the ATT after Analysis). It processes log records in **reverse LSN order** using a max-heap.

For each UPDATE record being undone:
1. Write a **CLR** (Compensation Log Record) with the `before_image` as the new `after_image` and `undo_next_lsn = record.prev_lsn`
2. Apply the `before_image` to restore the page
3. Push `record.prev_lsn` onto the heap to continue the chain

For CLR records: simply follow `undo_next_lsn` (the update was already undone)

When `undo_next_lsn == INVALID_LSN` (or we reach a BEGIN record), the transaction is fully undone — write an ABORT record.

**Why CLRs matter:** If the system crashes during Undo, the CLRs written so far tell the next recovery which undos were already completed, preventing double-undo.

functions.name: Undo(const vector<LogRecord>& logs)
functions.description: Roll back uncommitted transactions by traversing prev_lsn chains in reverse, writing CLRs.
hints: Build a `map<lsn_t, index>` for O(1) record lookup by LSN.
Use `priority_queue<lsn_t>` (max-heap) initialized with `att_[*].lastLSN`.
Pop largest LSN, find the record, handle based on type.
For UPDATE: write CLR with `undo_next = prev_lsn`, apply `before_image`.
For CLR: push `undo_next_lsn` if != INVALID_LSN.
For BEGIN: write ABORT record (txn fully undone).
Clear ATT when done.

hints: Start with the LogManager — AppendLog and ReadAllLogs are independent of recovery logic and easy to test.
Implement Analysis before Redo/Undo. Print ATT and DPT after Analysis to verify they match expectations.
For Redo: the key insight is the pageLSN check. If `pageLSN >= record.lsn`, the update was already on disk — skip it.
For Undo: use a max-heap (priority_queue) to process records in reverse LSN order across all active transactions simultaneously.
CLR records have `undo_next_lsn` pointing to the NEXT record to undo (i.e., `prev_lsn` of the UPDATE being undone). This lets recovery skip already-undone records if it crashes during Undo.
Draw the log as a timeline with arrows for prev_lsn chains. Trace through Analysis/Redo/Undo by hand before coding.
The Undo phase writes new log records (CLRs and ABORTs). These are appended to the same log file, making recovery idempotent.
Read Chapter 18 of the textbook (Crash Recovery) for the full ARIES algorithm. Our implementation simplifies some aspects (no fuzzy checkpoint, no nested top actions).
